title.narrative: Provision of integrated health, nutrition, and food security, and livelihood services IDPs and host communities in North Darfur.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThrough this proposed project, Relief International (RI) and its partners are to address the food crisis in El Fasher, an area categorized as IPC System 4, aiming to reach 133,712 individuals. This involves supporting increased food production and enhancing livelihood resilience among the affected populations. To achieve this, RI plans to distribute staple crop and vegetable seeds, as well as agriculture tool kits. RI is committed to ensuring that households with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM), and Severe Chronic (SC) cases are prioritized for the distribution of tools and seeds. Additionally, these households will be targeted for Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) awareness raising sessions, embedding crucial messages into all nutrition-related awareness and counseling sessions. In addition to addressing food insecurity, the project aims to improve access to healthcare by bolstering primary healthcare services, including emergency trauma response. RI will also focus on enhancing the capacity of health workers and collaborating with the State Ministry of Health (SMoH) to respond to disease outbreaks.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtSudan hosts the world's largest population of internally displaced persons, with over 6.5 million displaced internally and an additional 2 million seeking refuge in neighboring countries. The inability to move to safer areas is a major challenge for those trapped in high-conflict zones like Zamzam camp in El Fasher, worsened by the high cost of travel. While conflict has slightly decreased in some western areas, North Darfur has experienced an escalation. Conflict in primary crop areas during the harvest season has led to a 46% decrease in cereal production compared to the previous year, with up to 80% yield reductions in Greater Darfur. Despite functioning markets, food prices are 73% higher than last year and 350% above the five-year average, exacerbated by the devaluation of the Sudanese currency. About 70% of health facilities in conflict-affected areas are non-functional, burnt, or destroyed, with staff fleeing to safer areas, increasing the risk of death for displaced children and disease outbreaks such as measles, malaria, and cholera, which have reached 11,000 cases according to the Ministry of Health. Shortages of medical and nutrition supplies, limited access to clean water, sanitation, and hygiene services, and overburdened health services in IDP areas increase the risk of death from preventable or treatable diseases. Without an immediate halt to hostilities and significant deployment of humanitarian assistance, the population in Darfur faces the worst levels of acute food insecurity and malnutrition during the upcoming lean season from April to May 2024.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtRI aims to integrate conflict sensitivity into all its activities, involving comprehensive conflict analysis, adapting activities to the context, and adhering to the "do no harm" principle. This includes community engagement, transparent beneficiary selection, and risk assessment. Collaboration, monitoring and evaluation, staff training, feedback mechanisms, and flexible programming are key. The goal is to ensure activities don't escalate conflicts, but instead promote peace, stability, and provide timely assistance to vulnerable communities in conflict zones.ltbrgtlt/pgt
